core_obligations: Write the given projective module as a direct summand of a free module and lift its projector to a matrix, then form the characteristic polynomial f and the ring extension B = A[x]/(f) (proof lines 2028-2036).
Show that the image of f modulo each prime containing I is x^n times (x-1)^n, so that x(1-x) lies in every prime of B/IB and some power x^N(1-x)^N lies in IB (proof lines 2036-2045).
Use this to produce a canonical idempotent of the quotient B/IB and verify that it maps to the original projector under the action on the free module (proof lines 2045-2055).

Lift that idempotent along an etale extension provided by the idempotent lifting of the section, take its image in the endomorphism ring and define the lifted projective module as the image of the resulting idempotent (proof lines 2055-2063).
proof_roadmap: Produce the projector and the characteristic polynomial (proof lines 2028-2036).
Show the coprime powers condition modulo I (proof lines 2036-2045).
Build the idempotent of B/IB and match it with the projector (proof lines 2045-2055).
Lift the idempotent etale and define the module (proof lines 2055-2064).
difficulty_reason: The lemma refines the idempotent lifting of the same section to finite projective modules: a finite projective module modulo an ideal is the reduction of a finite projective module after passing to an etale extension that is an isomorphism modulo the ideal. The proof is a 37-line construction that writes the given projective module as a direct summand of a free module, lifts the projectors to a matrix, forms the characteristic polynomial of that matrix and the resulting finite ring extension, shows that the roots x and 1 - x of that polynomial are sufficiently coprime modulo the ideal so that a canonical element becomes an idempotent of the quotient, lifts that idempotent along an etale extension using the idempotent lifting of the section, and finally takes the image of the lifted idempotent to define the projective module. The two steps with real content are the production of the idempotent of the quotient through the characteristic polynomial and the appeal to idempotent lifting, and both are displayed.
